questions.question: The salary of an employee is increased by 5% in the first year and again by 5% in the second year. What is the overall percentage increase in the salary after two years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Percentage** formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, both first and second year increases are **5%**, so a = 5 and b = 5.

Net Increase = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5) ÷ 100

Net Increase = 10 + 0.25 = 10.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Assume the **Initial Salary** of the employee is 100 units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b50f88c69b8fa2e4326fc3cd86fc037d939ecf37568cbeeadbb65058e1182b2.png] 

⇒ Let initial salary = 100

⇒ Salary after 1st year = 100 + (5% of 100) = 100 + 5 = 105

⇒ Salary after 2ⁿd year = 105 + (5% of 105) = 105 + 5.25 = 110.25

⇒ Total **Percentage Increase** = ((110.25 − 100) ÷ 100) × 100 = 10.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Increase/Decrease

When a value changes by x% and then y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%. Use positive signs for increase and negative signs for decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

For a 5% increase, the multiplying factor is 1.05. For two successive 5% increases, the final value is Initial × 1.05 × 1.05 = Initial × 1.1025.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁d₂/100)]%.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 5. If their LCM is 240, what is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 4 : 5 → LCM of ratio parts = 4 × 5 = 20 units

Given **LCM** = 240 ⇒ 20 units = 240 ⇒ 1 unit = 12 (this is the **HCF**)

Sum of ratio parts = 4 + 5 = 9 units

Sum of numbers = 9 units × 12 = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = 4 : 5 and LCM = 240.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c2075552cba0394b01771085ace0659facd92fbd747f2292643bd08539198db.png] 

⇒ Let the two numbers be **4x** and **5x** (where x is the HCF).

⇒ LCM of 4x and 5x = 4 × 5 × x = 20x

⇒ 20x = 240

⇒ x = 240 ÷ 20 = 12

⇒ First number = 4 × 12 = 48

⇒ Second number = 5 × 12 = 60

⇒ **Sum of the numbers** = 48 + 60 = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers, Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.

HCF and LCM Relation

The HCF (Highest Common Factor) is always a **factor** of the LCM (Least Common Multiple).

LCM of Ratios

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b, then their **LCM** = a × b × HCF and their **Sum** = (a + b) × HCF.

questions.question: During a sale, 40% of the goods are sold at a profit of 10%. Of the remaining goods, 25% are sold at a profit of 15%, and the rest are sold at a loss of 29%. If there is an overall loss of x%, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of goods = 40 : (25% of 60) : (100 − 40 − 15) = 40 : 15 : 45 = 8 : 3 : 9.

Net change % = (Sum of weight × Value) ÷ Total weight

Net change % = (8 × 10 + 3 × 15 − 9 × 29) ÷ 20

Net change % = (80 + 45 − 261) ÷ 20 = −136 ÷ 20 = −6.8%.

Negative sign indicates loss, so **x = 6.8**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part 1 = **40%** of goods, Profit = **10%**

Part 2 = **25%** of remaining (60%) = **15%** of total, Profit = **15%**

Part 3 = **Rest** (100% − 40% − 15%) = **45%** of total, Loss = **29%**

**Formula Used:**

Overall Profit/Loss % = (Σ Percentage Part × Profit/Loss %) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c5739c4d98878a08193b9a38005e978b91fbe0a997a43a2505d00feba710cd7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total quantity be 100 units and CP per unit be 1.

⇒ Total CP = 100

⇒ Profit from 40 units = 40 × 10% = 4

⇒ Profit from 15 units = 15 × 15% = 2.25

⇒ Loss from 45 units = 45 × 29% = 13.05

⇒ Net Profit/Loss = 4 + 2.25 − 13.05

⇒ Net Profit/Loss = 6.25 − 13.05 = −6.8

⇒ **Overall Loss % = (6.8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 6.8%**

⇒ Comparing with **overall loss of x%**, we get **x = 6.8**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit/Loss

When goods are divided into different parts sold at different profit/loss rates, the overall result is the weighted average: Net % = (Σ nᵢ × rᵢ) ÷ (Σ nᵢ).

Relation between Loss and x

If a problem states an 'overall loss of x%', the value of x is always positive. The 'loss' keyword itself accounts for the negative sign of the net result.

Successive Percentage vs Weighted Average

Weighted average is used for different parts of a whole, whereas successive percentage change [x + y + (xy/100)] is used when changes occur on the same value one after another.

questions.question: The fourth proportional to 1.2, 4.8, and 7.15 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **scaling factor** between the first two terms: 4.8 ÷ 1.2 = 4.

Since the terms are in **proportion**, the same factor applies to the third and fourth terms.

Fourth proportional = 7.15 × 4 = 28.6.

**∴ The correct answer is 28.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 1.2

Second term (b) = 4.8

Third term (c) = 7.15

**Formula Used:**

If a, b, c, and d are in **proportion** (a : b :: c : d), then a × d = b × c.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed826476d72a374e7ebcd3d692cd6609453ac19adea1e0d5bc8a2efd4e1118d2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **fourth proportional** be d.

⇒ 1.2 : 4.8 :: 7.15 : d

⇒ 1.2 ÷ 4.8 = 7.15 ÷ d

⇒ 1 ÷ 4 = 7.15 ÷ d

⇒ d = 7.15 × 4

⇒ d = 28.6

**∴ The correct answer is 28.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is the third proportional, where c = b² ÷ a.

Product Rule of Proportion

In any proportion, the **Product of Extremes** (first and fourth terms) is always equal to the **Product of Means** (second and third terms).

Simplify:

 ((1.5 times 0.2))/(0.3)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly multiply 1.5 × 0.2 to get 0.3.

Divide the result by the **denominator** 0.3.

Simplification: 0.3 ÷ 0.3 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: ((1.5 × 0.2)) / 0.3

**Formula Used:**

Follow the **BODMAS** order of operations, starting with multiplication in the numerator followed by division.

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1.5 × 0.2) ÷ 0.3

⇒ 0.3 ÷ 0.3

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The rule defines the correct sequence: **Brackets**, **Of/Orders**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Decimal Multiplication

Multiply digits as whole numbers (15 × 2 = 30) and then shift the decimal point left by the total number of decimal places (1 + 1 = 2) to get 0.30.

Division of Decimals

Multiplying both the **numerator** and **denominator** by a power of 10 (like 10 or 100) can simplify the division by removing decimals.

questions.question: A rectangular garden has a length of 25 meters and a width of 18 meters. If a path of uniform width 2 meters is constructed around the outside of the garden, what is the perimeter of the outer edge of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **rectangular garden** of length L and width W with a **path of uniform width** w outside:

**Outer Perimeter** = 2 × (L + W) + 8w

⇒ Outer Perimeter = 2 × (25 + 18) + 8 × 2

⇒ Outer Perimeter = 2 × 43 + 16 = 86 + 16 = 102 m

**∴ The correct answer is 102 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of garden (L) = 25 m

Width of garden (W) = 18 m

Width of path (w) = 2 m (outside)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f19c2c94773c300bb5eb0aaf70772d6549be35b219a87e633163701776acf8c.png] 

When a path is constructed **outside**, it adds to the dimensions on both sides:

⇒ **Outer Length** = L + 2w = 25 + 2 × 2 = 29 m

⇒ **Outer Width** = W + 2w = 18 + 2 × 2 = 22 m

The **perimeter** of a rectangle is given by the formula: 2 × (Length + Width)

⇒ Perimeter of outer edge = 2 × (29 + 22)

⇒ Perimeter of outer edge = 2 × 51 = 102 m

**∴ The correct answer is 102 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Outer Path

The area of a path built outside a rectangle is calculated as: **Area** = (L + 2w)(W + 2w) − LW = 2w(L + W + 2w).

Area of Inner Path

If the path is built inside the garden, the **Inner Dimensions** become (L − 2w) and (W − 2w). Area = 2w(L + W − 2w).

Perimeter of Inner Path

The perimeter of the inner edge (when path is inside) is: **Perimeter** = 2(L + W − 4w) or 2 × (L + W) − 8w.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 36 days, respectively. Both work for 4 days and then A leaves. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 12 and 36) = **36 units**.

Efficiency of A = 3 units/day; Efficiency of B = 1 unit/day.

Combined efficiency = 3 + 1 = **4 units/day**.

Work done in 4 days = 4 × 4 = **16 units**.

Remaining work = 36 − 16 = **20 units**.

Days taken by B = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 12 days

Time taken by **B** = 36 days

Working duration together = 4 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **A + B** = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Work done by **A and B** in 4 days = 4 × 4 = 16 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = Total Work − Completed Work

⇒ Remaining Work = 36 − 16 = 20 units

⇒ **Time taken by B** = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 days

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work-Efficiency Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar logic applies where efficiency of inlet pipes is positive and outlet/leakage efficiency is negative.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of work done or the ratio of efficiencies when workers work for the same duration.

questions.question:
Simplify:

30 + [{-9 × (26 - 11 + 6)}]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule sequence: **Brackets** → **Multiplication** → **Addition**.

Solve inner parentheses first: (26 − 11 + 6) = 21.

Multiply by −9: −9 × 21 = −189.

Final calculation: 30 + (−189) = 30 − 189 = −159.

**∴ The correct answer is −159.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 30 + [{−9 × (26 − 11 + 6)}]

**Method Used:** **BODMAS/VBODMAS** Rule for order of operations.

⇒ Step 1: Simplify the value inside the **small brackets ()**.

⇒ (26 − 11 + 6) = 15 + 6 = 21

⇒ Step 2: Substitute this value back into the **braces {}**.

⇒ {−9 × 21} = −189

⇒ Step 3: Now the expression is 30 + [−189].

⇒ 30 − 189 = −159

**∴ The correct answer is −159.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order: **B**rackets, **O**rders (powers, roots, etc.), **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

Types of Brackets

The order of opening brackets is **Bar/Vinculum**, then **Parentheses ( )**, then **Braces { }**, and finally **Square Brackets [ ]**.

Integer Multiplication Rules

Multiplying a **positive** number by a **negative** number always results in a **negative** product (+ × − = −).

questions.question: A tank is normally filled by pipe A in 10 hours. Due to a leak, the tank takes 12 hours to fill. Find the time taken by the leak alone to empty a full tank.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When an **inlet pipe** takes T₁ hours and with a **leak** it takes T₂ hours:

Time taken by **leak alone** to empty = (T₁ × T₂) ÷ (T₂ − T₁)

Time = (10 × 12) ÷ (12 − 10)

Time = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 60 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling time of **Pipe A** = 10 hr

Filling time with **leakage** (A + Leak) = 12 hr

**Formula Used:**

Total Capacity = **LCM** of individual times

Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time

 **Efficiency (units/hr)**

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 6 units/hr

⇒ Net efficiency with **leak** = 5 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Leak alone** = 6 − 5 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Time taken by **leak** to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Leak Efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 60 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work Concept

In **pipes and cisterns**, an outlet pipe or a **leak** performs negative work, which reduces the overall efficiency of the filling system.

Net Efficiency Rule

If multiple pipes operate, the **net efficiency** is the algebraic sum of individual efficiencies (positive for inlet, negative for outlet).

Capacity and Time Relation

The **time** taken to fill or empty is inversely proportional to the **efficiency**: Time = Work ÷ Efficiency.

questions.question: If a sum of ₹70,000 amounts to ₹74,263 in X years under compound interest, compounded annually at 3% per annum, find X.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest earned = ₹74,263 − ₹70,000 = ₹4,263.

Total interest percentage = (4,263 ÷ 70,000) × 100 = 6.09%.

Using successive percentage for 3%: 3 + 3 + (3 × 3)/100 = 6.09%.

This matches for a time period of 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹70,000

**Amount (A)** = ₹74,263

**Rate (R)** = 3% p.a. compounded annually.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/805d46c6a5c28e02697752e5f749555f079e4d2d1a7ec0cc67a2c0c7a9bd36d0.png] 

The formula for **Amount (A)** under **Compound Interest** is:

A = P(1 + R/100)X

⇒ 74263 = 70000(1 + 3/100)X

⇒ 74263 ÷ 70000 = (1 + 0.03)X

⇒ 10609 ÷ 10000 = (1.03)X

⇒ 1.0609 = (1.03)X

⇒ (1.03)² = (1.03)X

⇒ X = 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount is given by A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per year.

Effective Interest Rate

For compounding annually, the effective rate for 2 years at r% is r + r + (r×r)/100.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is CI − SI = P(R/100)².

questions.question: If the third proportional to two numbers is 32 and the second number is 16, find the first number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **third proportional** (c) of two numbers a and b is given by the relation: c = b² ÷ a.

Given: **Second number** (b) = 16 and **Third proportional** (c) = 32.

Substituting values: 32 = 16² ÷ a ⇒ 32 = 256 ÷ a.

a = 256 ÷ 32 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Second number (b) = 16

Third proportional (c) = 32

Let the **first number** be a.

**Formula Used:**

If three numbers a, b, and c are in **continued proportion**, then a : b = b : c.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0a7848370b293e56be0a3fad1755d7bab0cbce0ea8a2d07bf10aa73cf9532d6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ a ÷ 16 = 16 ÷ 32

⇒ a × 32 = 16 × 16 (Product of extremes = Product of means)

⇒ 32a = 256

⇒ a = 256 ÷ 32

⇒ a = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers x and y is defined as √(x × y).

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then d is the **fourth proportional**, calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion Property

For three numbers to be in **continued proportion**, the middle term squared must equal the product of the first and third terms: b² = a × c.

questions.question: A store sells pens and notebooks. If 3 pens and 2 notebooks cost ₹120, and 2 pens and 4 notebooks cost ₹140, what is the price of one notebook?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the number of **pens** by multiplying the first set by 2 and the second set by 3.

First Set: 6 **Pens** + 4 **Notebooks** = ₹240

Second Set: 6 **Pens** + 12 **Notebooks** = ₹420

Difference: 8 **Notebooks** = ₹180

Price of 1 **Notebook** = 180 ÷ 8 = ₹22.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹22.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 **pens** and 2 **notebooks** = ₹120

Cost of 2 **pens** and 4 **notebooks** = ₹140

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e5efd28db89c1c101e03ef2ce63e53c8ea6d08f4cfcb3b3a24b86bebc34ee75.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the price of one **pen** be P and one **notebook** be N.

⇒ 3P + 2N = 120 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ 2P + 4N = 140 --- (Eq. 2)

⇒ From (Eq. 2), simplify by dividing by 2: P + 2N = 70

⇒ Express P in terms of N: P = 70 − 2N

⇒ Substitute P in (Eq. 1): 3 × (70 − 2N) + 2N = 120

⇒ 210 − 6N + 2N = 120

⇒ 210 − 4N = 120

⇒ 4N = 210 − 120

⇒ 4N = 90

⇒ N = 90 ÷ 4 = 22.50

questions.question: In genetics, a gene refers to which of the following?

options.text: A section of DNA that codes for a protein

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A section of DNA that codes for a protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **gene** is the fundamental physical and functional unit of **heredity**, consisting of a specific sequence of **nucleotides** in **DNA** (or **RNA** in some viruses).
 
• In molecular genetics, a gene is defined as a segment of **DNA** that contains the necessary instructions to synthesize a **functional product**, which is usually a **protein** or a functional **RNA** molecule.
 
• The process of decoding a gene begins with **transcription**, where the DNA sequence is copied into **messenger RNA (mRNA)**, followed by **translation**, where the **ribosome** uses the mRNA template to assemble **amino acids** into a **polypeptide chain**.
 
• Genes are located at specific positions called **loci** (singular: **locus**) on **chromosomes**, and they act as the blueprint for an organism's **phenotypic traits**, such as eye color or enzyme production.
 
• Structurally, eukaryotic genes are composed of **exons** (coding regions), **introns** (non-coding intervening sequences), and **regulatory sequences** like **promoters** and **enhancers** that control when and how a gene is expressed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chromosomes and Sex Chromosomes**:

 
 
• A **chromosome** is a thread-like structure made of **DNA** and **histone proteins** that carries hundreds or thousands of genes; it is the container for genes, not the gene itself.
 
• **Sex chromosomes** (such as **X** and **Y** in humans) are a specific category of chromosomes that determine biological sex and carry sex-linked genes.
 
 
 
• **Blood Groups**:
 
 
• Blood groups like **ABO** and **Rh** are **phenotypes** or inherited traits determined by the expression of specific **alleles** (variant forms of a gene) located on **Chromosome 9** and **Chromosome 1** respectively.
 
 
 
• **Genotype and Alleles**:
 
 
• The term **genotype** refers to the actual genetic makeup of an individual, while **alleles** are different versions of the same gene that can lead to variations in inherited characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following memory types is non-volatile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-volatile memory** is a type of computer memory that has the capability to hold saved data even if the power supply is turned off.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a prominent example of non-volatile memory because it stores critical start-up instructions, such as the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)**, which must remain intact every time the computer is powered on.
 
• Data stored in **ROM** is generally written during the manufacturing process or through specialized methods, ensuring that the **firmware** and essential operating instructions are not lost during a system crash or power failure.
 
• In contrast to **RAM**, which is used for temporary data processing, **ROM** serves as a permanent storage medium for the core functional code of electronic devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)**:

 
 
• Identified as **volatile memory**, meaning all data stored in it is wiped clean immediately when the power is disconnected.
 
• It serves as the **primary memory** where the system loads the **operating system** and active applications for high-speed access by the processor.
 
 
 
• **CPU (Central Processing Unit)**:
 
 
• Known as the **brain of the computer**, it is the electronic circuitry that executes instructions of a computer program.
 
• While it contains internal high-speed storage units like **registers** and **Cache**, the **CPU** itself is a processing unit rather than a memory type.
 
 
 
• **PCB (Printed Circuit Board)**:
 
 
• A **PCB** is the foundational hardware component that mechanically supports and electrically connects various electronic parts using **conductive tracks**.
 
• It is not a form of memory storage but rather the **motherboard** or circuit carrier for components like the **CPU** and **RAM**.

questions.question: Which metal reacts violently with cold water, producing a metal hydroxide, hydrogen gas, and enough heat for the hydrogen to catch fire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** is a highly reactive **alkali metal** located in **Group 1** of the periodic table, characterized by having a single valence electron which it loses very easily.
 
• When placed in **cold water**, it undergoes an instantaneous and **violent chemical reaction** to produce **Potassium Hydroxide** (a strong base) and **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• The reaction is categorized as highly **exothermic**, meaning it releases a massive amount of **thermal energy** in a very short duration.
 
• The heat generated during this process is so intense that it immediately reaches the **ignition temperature** of the liberated **Hydrogen gas**, causing it to catch fire and burn with a distinctive **lilac (pale violet) flame** due to the presence of **potassium ions**.
 
• The chemical representation of this reaction is: 2K(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2KOH(aq) + H₂(g) + **Heat energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series Comparison:**

 
 
• **Sodium**: Similar to potassium, it reacts vigorously with **cold water** and the hydrogen often catches fire (burning with a **yellow flame**), though it is slightly less reactive than potassium.
 
• **Calcium**: It reacts with **cold water** to form **Calcium Hydroxide** and hydrogen, but the reaction is less violent and the heat produced is **insufficient** to ignite the hydrogen gas. The metal often floats because **bubbles of hydrogen** stick to its surface.
 
• **Magnesium**: It does not react with **cold water** at all; it requires **hot water** or **steam** to react, forming magnesium hydroxide or magnesium oxide.
 
• **Aluminium**: This metal does not react with cold or hot water due to a stable, protective **Aluminium Oxide layer** on its surface, though it will react with **steam** at high temperatures.

questions.question: The 106th Constitutional Amendment inserted which of the following new Articles in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**330A, 332A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023**, officially known as the **Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023** or the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, marks a historic shift in Indian legislative representation by mandating **33 percent reservation** for women.
 
• The Act inserted **Article 330A** into the Constitution to provide for the reservation of seats for women in the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha). This includes a sub-reservation for women belonging to the **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** within the seats already reserved for those categories.
 
• The Act also inserted **Article 332A**, which extends the **one-third reservation** for women to the **Legislative Assemblies** of every State in India, ensuring gender-balanced representation at the state level.
 
• Furthermore, **Article 334A** was added to specify the commencement of these provisions. The reservation will be implemented after the first **census** conducted after the Act's commencement and the subsequent **delimitation** exercise is completed.
 
• The amendment modified **Article 239AA** of the Constitution to ensure that the reservation policy also applies to the **Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Background**:

 
 
• The bill was introduced as the **Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023**, during a special session of Parliament.
 
• It received **Presidential assent** on **September 28, 2023**, following nearly unanimous support in both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The primary objective is to enhance women's participation in **policy-making** and governance at the national and state levels.
 
 
 
• **Operational Features**:
 
 
• The reservation is mandated for a period of **15 years** from the date of its commencement, though it can be extended by a law passed by **Parliament**.
 
• Seats reserved for women shall be allocated by **rotation** to different constituencies within a State or Union Territory as determined by Parliament.
 
• This amendment fulfills a long-standing demand for women's quotas that had been pending in various forms for nearly **three decades**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the social structure of Mauryan society in ancient India?

options.text: A completely egalitarian society without any form of social or occupational differentiation
An organised society with distinct social classes and a wide range of occupational groups
Society controlled only by mercantile guilds with no other social groups
Exclusively tribal society with absence of settled agriculture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An organised society with distinct social classes and a wide range of occupational groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mauryan society** was characterized by a sophisticated and hierarchical structure as documented in contemporary literature like **Megasthenes' Indika** and **Kautilya's Arthashastra**.
 
• **Megasthenes**, the Greek ambassador in the court of **Chandragupta Maurya**, observed that the society was divided into **seven distinct classes**: philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers, and councillors, primarily categorized by their functional roles in the state.
 
• While the traditional **Varna system** (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras) remained the ideological foundation, the era saw the proliferation of various **Jatis** (sub-castes) arising from the integration of tribal groups and occupational specialization.
 
• The state exercised significant control over social life, with **Kautilya** emphasizing the duties of different classes to maintain **Dharma** and social stability within the vast **Mauryan Empire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Social Hierarchy and Governance:**

 
 
• Contrary to being an **egalitarian society**, the **Mauryan** period featured sharp socio-economic disparities; the **Brahmins** and **Kshatriyas** occupied the top tier, while **Shudras** and **untouchables** were at the bottom.
 
• The economy was predominantly agrarian, but the rise of **urban centers** like **Pataliputra**, **Taxila**, and **Ujjain** facilitated the growth of powerful **mercantile guilds (Srenis)** that regulated trade and crafts.
 
• Ancient India during this period had moved far beyond an **exclusively tribal society**; it was the era of the first great centralized empire with a professional **standing army** and a complex **bureaucracy**.
 
• Evidence from **Ashokan Edicts** suggests a society where moral conduct and religious tolerance were promoted through the policy of **Dhamma**, aimed at unifying a diverse population.
 
• The status of **women** was varied; while they had certain rights to property (**Stridhana**), the society remained largely patriarchal, though some women served as **guards** or **spies** for the king.

questions.question: Which type of climate characterises the Great Indian Desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arid and semi arid climate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Great Indian Desert**, also known as the **Thar Desert**, is located in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent, primarily covering the state of **Rajasthan**.
 
• The region is characterized by an **Arid and semi arid climate** where the annual rainfall is extremely low, generally remaining below **25 cm** or **250 mm**.
 
• The climate is marked by a high **diurnal range of temperature**, where daytime temperatures in summer can soar above **45°C** while night temperatures can drop significantly.
 
• High rates of **evapotranspiration** and low humidity levels prevent the retention of moisture, resulting in sparse vegetation dominated by **xerophytic** plants and thorny bushes.
 
• The **Aravalli Range** plays a crucial role in creating these conditions as it lies parallel to the **Southwest Monsoon** winds, causing them to pass over the region without shedding much moisture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equatorial climate**:

 
 
• Features high temperatures and heavy **convectional rainfall** exceeding 200 cm throughout the year, found near the **Equator**.
 
 
 
• **Humid subtropical climate**:
 
 
• Characterized by hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters, typically found in the **Indo-Gangetic Plains** of Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Tropical monsoon climate**:
 
 
• Defined by seasonal reversal of winds and distinct **wet and dry seasons**, covering much of coastal and central India.
 
 
 
• **Luni River**:
 
 
• The only significant river in the **Thar Desert**, which is ephemeral and disappears into the **Rann of Kutch**.

questions.question: Which of the following features characterises Stage III of demographic transition?

options.text: High migration and low death rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low fertility and low mortality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Demographic Transition Model** (DTM) describes the historical shift from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as societies progress through **industrialization** and **urbanization**.
 
• **Stage III**, often referred to as the **Late Expanding** stage, is characterized by a significant decline in the **fertility rate** (birth rate) and a continued low or declining **mortality rate** (death rate).
 
• In this stage, the **natural increase** of the population begins to slow down because the gap between birth rates and death rates narrows.
 
• Social changes such as increased **female literacy**, higher **status of women**, and improved access to **contraception** and **family planning** services lead to smaller family sizes.
 
• Economic shifts from agricultural to **industrial** and **service-based economies** make children an economic liability rather than an asset, further driving down the birth rate.
 
• As per **NCERT** and standard geographical models, by the end of this stage, the society becomes highly **urbanized** and **literate**, with the population becoming stable or increasing very slowly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stage I (High Stationary)**:

 
 
• Characterized by **High Fertility** and **High Mortality**.
 
• Population growth is very slow because high birth rates are offset by high death rates caused by **epidemics**, **famines**, and lack of medical technology.
 
 
 
• **Stage II (Early Expanding)**:
 
 
• Features a **High Birth Rate** and a **Rapidly Declining Death Rate**.
 
• The improvement in **sanitation**, **healthcare**, and **food security** leads to a **population explosion** during this phase.
 
 
 
• **Migration**:
 
 
• While not a defining metric of DTM stages, **Rural-to-Urban Migration** typically peaks during Stage II and Stage III as the labor force moves toward industrial centers.
 
 
 
• **Stage IV (Low Stationary)**:
 
 
• Both birth and death rates are **very low**, leading to a stable or even declining population in some developed nations.

__
 
• The **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, popularly known as the **Rowlatt Act**, was passed by the **Imperial Legislative Council** in **March 1919**.
 
• This legislation granted the British colonial government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed the **detention of political prisoners without trial** for a duration of up to **two years**.
 
• Despite the **unanimous opposition** of Indian members within the council, such as **Madan Mohan Malaviya**, **Mazhar-ul-Haq**, and **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** (who resigned in protest), the bill was hurried through.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** criticized the act as 'unjust', 'tyrannical', and a 'Black Act' that violated fundamental civil rights, prompting him to form the **Satyagraha Sabha** to organize a nationwide protest.

• **Consequences**:
 
 
• The intense anti-Rowlatt agitation in the **Punjab** region led to the arrest of leaders like **Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew** and **Dr. Satyapal**.

questions.question: Which type(s) of Legislatures can a state have under the Indian Constitution?

__
 
• According to **Article 168** of the **Indian Constitution**, every state shall have a legislature which consists of the **Governor** and either one or two houses.
 
• A **Unicameral Legislature** refers to a system with only one house, known as the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha). The majority of Indian states currently function under this system.
 
• A **Bicameral Legislature** consists of two houses: the **Legislative Assembly** (Lower House) and the **Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad or Upper House).
 
• The Constitution provides flexibility, allowing states to have different structures based on their specific needs and historical context. Currently, six states possess a bicameral setup: **Andhra Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **Karnataka**, **Maharashtra**, **Telangana**, and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The **Parliament of India** has the authority to create or abolish the **Legislative Council** in a state under **Article 169**, provided the state’s **Legislative Assembly** passes a resolution to that effect with a **special majority**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)**

 
 
• It is the popular house where members are **directly elected** by the people for a term of **five years**.
 
• The maximum strength is capped at **500** members, while the minimum is generally **60**, though exceptions exist for smaller states like **Sikkim** and **Goa**.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)**
 
 
• It is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every **two years**.
 
• The total number of members in the Council cannot exceed **one-third** of the total membership of the Assembly but must not be less than **40**.
 
• Members are elected through a complex process involving **Local Bodies**, **Graduates**, **Teachers**, and nomination by the **Governor**.

__
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** (IVC) was primarily a secular and egalitarian society where urban planning prioritized **civic amenities** over the glorification of rulers or deities.
 
• Unlike contemporary civilizations in **Egypt** (known for **Pyramids**) or **Mesopotamia** (known for **Ziggurats**), Harappan sites lack evidence of **monumental palaces**, **royal tombs**, or massive religious temples.
 
• The architectural focus was strictly **utilitarian** and **functional**, emphasizing public health, sanitation, and efficient resource storage rather than aesthetic ornamentation or grand monuments.
 
• Harappan cities were divided into a raised **Citadel** for public buildings and a **Lower Town** for residential quarters, reflecting a highly organized social structure based on administrative or trade needs rather than hereditary monarchy.
 
• Structural remains like the **Great Bath** at **Mohenjo-Daro** and the **Granaries** at **Harappa** served communal purposes, confirming that architecture was geared toward the welfare of the general population.

• **Standardized Construction Materials**:

 
 
• The Harappans used **standardized baked bricks** with a fixed ratio of **1:2:4** (thickness to width to length), which was consistent across hundreds of miles from **Kalibangan** to **Lothal**.
 
• While sun-dried bricks were common in other cultures, the IVC is unique for its extensive use of **kiln-fired bricks**, ensuring the longevity of structures.

• Cities featured a **grid system** where streets ran north-south and east-west, intersecting at 90-degree angles.
 
• Every house was connected to a sophisticated **underground drainage system** lined with bricks and provided with removable stone slabs for cleaning, representing the highest standard of **sanitary engineering** in the ancient world.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Architecture**:
 
 
• Houses were built with several rooms around a **central courtyard**, often featuring private wells and separate **bathing areas**, showcasing a high level of privacy and comfort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• When **dilute Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** reacts with **Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (NaHCO₃)**, it undergoes a chemical reaction where the acid decomposes the bicarbonate.
 
• The general chemical principle is that the reaction between an **acid** and a **metal hydrogen carbonate** always produces a **salt**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide gas**.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: **HCl (aq) + NaHCO₃ (s) → NaCl (aq) + H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g)**.
 
• In this specific process, **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is the salt formed in the solution, and the gas evolved is **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)**, which causes **brisk effervescence**.

• It is widely utilized in **fire extinguishers** and the carbonation of beverages.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (NaHCO₃)**:
 
 
• Commonly known as **Baking Soda**, it acts as a mild base.

questions.question: A computer cannot open a printer without a driver. This driver is an example of a/an:

• A **Device Driver** is a specialized type of **System Software** that acts as an essential **interface** between the computer's **Operating System (OS)** and the hardware components attached to it.
 
• The primary function of a driver is to translate high-level commands from the **OS** or an **Application** into the specific low-level machine language instructions that the hardware, such as a **Printer**, can interpret and execute.
 
• Since **System Software** is defined as the programs that manage the resources of the computer system and provide a platform for application software, drivers are categorized here because the system cannot interact with peripheral hardware without them.
 
• When a user sends a print command, the **Printer Driver** converts the document's data into a format specific to the printer's **Control Language** (e.g., **PostScript** or **PCL**), ensuring the hardware functions as intended.
 
• Most modern operating systems use **Kernel-mode** drivers for stability, allowing the driver to have direct access to system memory and hardware registers to manage data flow efficiently.

• **Input Device**:
 
 
• This refers to physical **Hardware** components used to provide data and control signals to an information processing system. Common examples include the **Keyboard**, **Mouse**, and **Scanner**.

• The **cranium** is composed of **eight specific cranial bones** that are joined together by immovable fibrous joints called **sutures**, creating a rigid, shock-resistant vault.
 
• This rigid shell protects vital neural components, including the **cerebrum**, **cerebellum**, and **brainstem**, from mechanical injuries and external pressure.

• Its core biological function is to protect the **spinal cord** and provide **axial support** for the body weight.
 
 
 
• **Pelvic girdle**
 
 
• Composed of the **hip bones** (ilium, ischium, and pubis) and connects the **axial skeleton** to the lower limbs.

• **STL**, which stands for **Stereolithography**, is the most widely used file format for **3D printing** and **Rapid Prototyping**. It was originally created by **3D Systems** in **1987** for their computer-aided design (CAD) software.
 
• The format functions by describing the **surface geometry** of a three-dimensional object through a process known as **tessellation**. It uses a series of linked **triangles** (facets) to approximate the surfaces of a solid model.
 
• It is considered a universal language for **3D printers** because it provides the raw geometric data that **slicing software** requires to generate **G-code**, which guides the printer's nozzle or laser.
 
• One defining characteristic of an **STL file** is that it only contains information about the **shape** and **geometry**. It does not store data regarding **color**, **texture**, **material**, or internal structures.
 
• The **resolution** of the 3D model in this format is determined by the number of triangles used; a higher count of **triangles** results in a smoother surface but a larger file size.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes ROM from RAM?

options.text: ROM is used for storage; RAM is used for graphics.
ROM is volatile; RAM is non-volatile.
ROM stores permanent instructions; RAM stores temporary data.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM stores permanent instructions; RAM stores temporary data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a type of **non-volatile memory**, meaning it retains its stored information even after the power supply is turned off. It is primarily used to store the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** and other essential **firmware** required to boot the computer. Hence, it stores **permanent instructions**.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a **volatile memory** device, which means all stored data is lost once the power is disconnected. It serves as the **primary memory** where the **operating system**, application programs, and data in current use are kept so they can be quickly reached by the **CPU**. Hence, it stores **temporary data**.
 
• The fundamental distinction lies in their **persistence** and **functionality**: ROM handles the startup process and fixed system instructions, while RAM facilitates the **real-time execution** of active tasks and multitasking.
 
• While **RAM** allows for both **reading and writing** at high speeds, standard **ROM** is traditionally limited to reading, although modern variants like **Flash memory** have evolved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Memory**:

 
 
• **RAM Varieties**: Includes **SRAM (Static RAM)**, which is faster and used for **cache**, and **DRAM (Dynamic RAM)**, which is slower and used for main system memory.
 
• **ROM Varieties**: Includes **PROM (Programmable ROM)**, **EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM)**, and **EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM)**.
 
 
 
• **Performance Characteristics**:
 
 
• **Speed**: **RAM** is significantly faster than ROM, allowing the processor to access data in **nanoseconds**.
 
• **Capacity**: Modern systems require large amounts of **RAM (e.g., 8GB, 16GB)** to run software, whereas **ROM** chips are much smaller in capacity.

__
 
• The **New Industrial Policy (NIP)** was announced on **July 24, 1991**, under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, marking the beginning of **economic reforms** in India.
 
• The core objective of the policy was to dismantle the **License Raj**, which was a system of licenses, regulations, and accompanying red tape that hindered industrial growth and private enterprise.
 
• A major feature of this policy was the **abolition of industrial licensing** for all projects, irrespective of the level of investment, except for a short list of **18 industries** related to security, strategic concerns, and social reasons.
 
• This reform aimed to enhance industrial efficiency and international competitiveness by allowing entrepreneurs to make production decisions based on **market signals** rather than government directives.
 
• The policy also drastically reduced the number of industries reserved exclusively for the **Public Sector** from **17** to just **8**, opening up crucial sectors like **mining**, **telecommunications**, and **transport** to private investment.
 
• It introduced the concept of **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** to integrate the Indian economy with the global market and attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalization**:

 
 
• Removal of restrictive **trade barriers** and government intervention in the economy.
 
• Simplification of **export-import** procedures and rationalization of **tax structures**.
 
• Currently, only **five industries** require compulsory licensing, including **electronic aerospace**, **gunpowder/explosives**, and **hazardous chemicals**.
 
 
 
• **Privatization**:
 
 
• Involves **disinvestment**, where the government sells its equity in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** to private entities or the general public.
 
• It aims to improve the managerial efficiency and financial discipline of enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Globalization**:
 
 
• Encouraged the entry of **Multinational Corporations (MNCs)** through **Automatic Approval** routes for foreign technology agreements.
 
• Established the **Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB)** to negotiate with international firms and facilitate **FDI** inflows.
 
 
 
• **MRTP Act**:
 
 
• The 1991 policy scrapped the requirement for **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP)** companies to seek prior approval for expansion or establishment of new undertakings.
